scope: Only the two specified complete replacement help paragraphs. Prior reviews, the exact English, all complete target clauses and primary grammatical/technical evidence were read. No repository edits or modifications to candidates.

entries.source: Set the top-left corner of this image on the output canvas. X and Y are whole pixels, starting at zero. Other images keep their current positions. Overlap is allowed here; images imported later are drawn on top. The canvas expands to include all placed images. Crops and sizes stay unchanged.
entries.target: 출력 캔버스에서 이 이미지의 왼쪽 위 모서리 위치를 정헙서. X영 Y는 0서 시작허는 정수 픽셀 값이우다. 다른 이미지의 위치는 바꾸지 안헙네다. 이디서는 이미지가 겹쳐도 뒙네다. 나중에 불러온 이미지를 먼저 불러온 이미지 위에 그립네다. 놓은 이미지가 몬딱 들어가게 캔버스를 더 크게 헙네다. 잘라낸 범위영 크기는 바꾸지 안헙네다.
entries.note: The replacement is acceptable as a continuous modern technical-loan Jeju help paragraph. Its discourse moves from one user command to coordinates and application behavior, with consistent polite narration. The decision is based on the complete new wording and its grammatical dependencies, not merely on seven recoverable English facts or the author's clause audit.
connected_language_assessment: The opening imperative 정헙서 instructs the user. Copular 값이우다 then defines X/Y, while subsequent -ㅂ네다 clauses explain routine behavior. This change of speech act is coherent, and the later clauses do not read as additional commands.

In 다른 이미지의 위치는 바꾸지 안헙네다, 는 topicalizes the affected positions. The unspoken application subject is consistent with the later active rendering and canvas-enlargement clauses. The negative predicate states non-modification rather than forbidding a later user edit. The same construction closes the paragraph for crop extents and sizes.

The active object-plus-spatial-complement sequence 나중에 불러온 이미지를 먼저 불러온 이미지 위에 그립네다 is grammatical and makes the two import times explicit. Repetition of 이미지 is useful here: the earlier image is the surface-relative complement and the later image is the rendered object. It is not a command to move the later image upward.

놓은 이미지가 몬딱 들어가게 is a complete result/purpose clause, followed by 캔버스를 더 크게 헙네다. The overt object of enlargement is the canvas. The all-images quantifier has clear scope over the placed images, and the next sentence rules out image resizing. This resolves the old compressed containment/inchoative concern.

The familiar technical nouns form a loanword UI register. Shared Korean vocabulary alone is not proof of Jeju idiom; acceptance here also rests on the Jeju coordination, copula, imperative, negation and polite descriptive sequence. No demand for an unattested exact paragraph in a corpus was imposed.

entries.target: གཟུགས་བརྙན་འདི་གི་གཡོན་མགོའི་ཟུར་འདི་ གྲུབ་འབྲས་ཀྱི་འབྲི་གཞི་ནང་བཞག། X དང་ Y འདི་པིག་སེལ་གྱི་གྱངས་ཁ་ཨིནམ་དང་ ཧྲིལ་གྲངས་སྦེ་ 0 ལས་འགོ་བཙུགསཔ་ཨིན། གཟུགས་བརྙན་གཞན་ཚུ་ རང་རང་གི་ད་ལྟོའི་ས་གནས་ནང་རང་སྡོདཔ་ཨིན། ནཱ་ལུ་གཟུགས་བརྙན་ཚུ་གཅིག་གི་ཐོག་ཁར་གཅིག་བཞག་ཆོག། ཤུལ་ལས་ནང་འདྲེན་འབད་མི་གཟུགས་བརྙན་ཚུ་ ཧེ་མའི་གཟུགས་བརྙན་ཚུ་གི་ཐོག་ཁར་འབྲིཝ་ཨིན། བཞག་ཚར་མི་གཟུགས་བརྙན་ཆ་མཉམ་ཤོང་ནིའི་དོན་ལུ་ འབྲི་གཞི་གི་ཚད་རྒྱ་བསྐྱེད་འབདཝ་ཨིན། བཏོག་ཁུལ་དང་ཚད་ཚུ་མི་བསྒྱུར།
entries.note: The replacement is acceptable as a complete explanatory Dzongkha paragraph at moderate idiom confidence. The revised coordinate sentence supplies an actual count noun, and the expansion sentence now has an explicit purpose and a definite object of enlargement. Reading those clauses together removes the earlier composition hold; no new correction is required for the exact reviewed bytes.
connected_language_assessment: The opening placement command and the following explanatory sentences form a coherent instruction sequence. Image, image corner, canvas, other images and already-placed images retain distinct referents; the paragraph does not shift the placement anchor to the image center or canvas corner.

The coordinate sentence first predicates pixel count of X and Y, then describes those values as whole numbers beginning at 0. The count head avoids treating X/Y as physical pixel objects. The adverbial whole-number qualification is attached to the same coordinated subject and does not request rounding.

The other-images clause is a state-of-remaining statement. Its distributive possessive and emphatic location wording establish that each other image stays where it currently is. The following permission is locally limited by here and does not impose mandatory stacking.

Later-imported images are the rendered items, while the earlier images are the overt on-top-of complement. The implicit rendering agent is coherent in software help. The factual narration is not an instruction that the user manually draw or move the images.

The all-placed-images-fit clause now precedes an expanded purpose expression. The canvas's size is the object of expansion; it is no longer a compressed canvas-does-expansion juxtaposition. The closing negative-change clause naturally returns to image crop regions and image sizes. It does not negate the immediately stated growth of the canvas.

Output/result drawing surface and crop region are literal but usable technical compounds in this context. The paragraph is explanatory translated UI prose rather than conversational Dzongkha; that register is consistent throughout. Exact-phrase corpus attestation is not asserted.

clause_audit.note: The possessive chain identifies this image's left-upper corner; the output drawing surface is its destination.

Each other image stays at its own current location.
One over another is permitted, not required.

clause_audit.note: The later import modifier and earlier-image complement preserve stacking order.

limits: Moderate source-assisted idiom confidence, not native-speaker certification. No claim is made that the newly composed full paragraph occurs in a published source.
LibreOffice target-language passages were used only where Tibetan-script Dzongkha text was present; English fallback sentences were not counted as Dzongkha prose evidence.
No decision relies on corrupt Tibetan extraction from the computer-terms dictionary.

integration_rule: Acceptance applies only to the exact target_sha256 in each entry. Rewording requires independent full-value review of the new hash. These linguistic decisions do not certify Android layout, font shaping, runtime behavior or other locale values.
